I've been meaning to dabble in bitcoin for ages. Just, you know, salt a little away every month. I haven't had the slightest idea how to go about it, though, and I'm terrified of doing something stupid.

I started to set myself up with a Coinbase account today and I get as far as the identity questions and it insists I have my ID ready without specifying what ID to use. Hm. Okay. So I get on their livechat and the guy says "passport is best."

Yipe. I don't know why, but that gives me the willies. I realize my bank copied my passport, and my employer did (I'm an immigrant), but somehow the idea of scanning my passport and flinging it onto the internet makes me break out in hives.

Also, when I said my passport was in my maiden name but I've since married, would that be a problem? he repeated "passport is best." Making me think I was talking to a bot or stupid person.

Advice, please. Is this standard? I can't think why it would be unsafe, but it feels unsafe. Is there a better service to use? I don't have enough money to do stupid things with the money I've got.

Go grab some xbt on localbitcoins.com. Do it with a bank transfer for speed or face to face if you prefer (no id at all). You need a wallet ready ... i'd install one on your phone rather than use the coinbase one. That would take you all of 5 mins (recommend mycelium).

Over the long term, localbitcoins will probably be a bit expensive, but at least it gets you going. Then decide if you want to go the whole coinbase verification route.

Yes it is standard. Exchanges have to comply with basically the same regulations as banks these days. I don't know where you are, but in Canada the Bitcoin ATMs do not require ID (yet). I don't know about the name change. He said passport was best, but that doesn't mean much of anything. Use your drivers licencse and it should be just fine I think.

Coinbase has been one of the best and most reliable exchanges around. That being said they still control your keys so go ahead and finish the verification process and buy your Bitcoin, but once you have the Bitcoin I'd recommend putting the Bitcoin in a wallet like Electrum where you control the keys. And remember to back up the seed! Let me know if you have more questions, I'd be happy to guide you through the process.

Any USD-BTC gateway that uses the banking system (other than making a cash deposit into someone's account via localbitcoins) is going to want to see ID. Coinbase is pretty reputable. I do second the advice to put the BTC in your own wallet once you buy them from Coinbase (or any exchange).

The funeral home at the time that I was working at was a converted house. Because we were small we didn't have the luxury of large freezers like larger funeral homes or the county morgue. We had this 2 body freezer that looks sort of like an over-sized file cabinet that lived in the garage with the hearse. We had another single body freezer in the kitchen. The kitchen was the original kitchen of the house which was converted into the embalming room – we still called it the kitchen. (Yeah, dark humour).

I am alone as my two coworkers went on a body pick up. We have no clients scheduled for this morning, but we have a service in the afternoon. So it's on me to prep the body for this afternoon's viewing.

Usually this isn't a problem. I've done it a ton of times before myself. Just another day…

So I check the paperwork, gown up, glove up and hit the freezer. I pull out the top body, check the bag tag, check the paperwork, and open the bag to check the body tag and it's not the body I am looking for.

I move on to the second drawer and pull the drawer out – or I try to. The drawer is squeaking in protest, pulling on it is a huge effort, even with well-oiled rollers. The body bag is catching against the inside of the freezer and other than the small lip of the drawer that I am pulling on; all I see is the huge white mass of the body bag. I end up doing a weird squat pull maneuver just the lug the drawer out to be able to see the bag tag.

At this point, I'm annoyed. There is no air conditioning in the garage, it's easily over 100F outside and I've got a wool suit on under my embalming gown.

I check the bag tag against the paperwork and it matches, so I open up the bag to see a disgusting land whale inside. The ankle tag - his toes were so fat I don't think they could have fit the band between them - also matched.

I am now hot, uncomfortable, annoyed, and angry.

I’m angry because here I am, about 5’6 120lbs, stuck moving this blubber corpse that has to easily be 400lbs. My coworkers on the body run are men, both are about 6’4 and fit – one even moonlights as a stripper on his off shifts – in fact he picked this body up the day before so he KNEW.

And while we play pranks on each other, this isn’t a fun(ny) one. I probably shouldn’t be doing shit until they get back but I am stubborn and I hate sitting around idle.

I go back inside, remove my gloves and gown, remove my wool suit jacket, remove my button down shirt and put my gown back over the tank top I wear under my dress shirt. I also grab a new pair of gloves and the gurney from the kitchen. I am so happy to be in the blissful sub-zero air conditioning inside.

Begrudgingly, I roll the gurney down the ramp in the garage and line it up next to the freezer drawer where I collapse it. The gurney is still a couple of inches higher than the drawer and the drawer is like a shallow bowl.

With a normal sized human, even dead weight (haha), at this point I can just squat down, take a hold of the body bag and with minimal effort drag the bag up from the freezer drawer and onto the gurney.

Much to my dismay this wasn’t a normal sized human. I try my standard method but nothing really happens except I lose my grip on the bag and fall back onto my ass. Thus, I must find a new method.

Yes, I should have stopped and waited but I had no idea how long the body run my coworkers were on would take and now I am angry and determined to get this done.

I try to split up the work. I’m able to lug the feet up onto the gurney with a lot of yelling and cursing the fleas of a thousand camels into my coworker’s pubes but damn it, I got those feet up on the gurney and that’s like half the battle right?

Since that worked so well I try to do the same thing with the top half. Aaand all the blubber in the middle is stopping me.

Stopping I glare at the dead fattie and think. Then I sit down across from the body bag with my back against the tires of the hearse, put my feet at the middle and shove as hard as I can and the fat unsticks! HURRAY for progress!!!

I then proceed to shove as much of the body at least onto the gurney, pausing to tug in places when necessary.

After about a good 45 minutes to an hour I finally have this sack of fat on the gurney. I close the freezer, sweating like I don’t even know what at this point. I’m still angry, though that anger helped me to hulk out and shove the guy so it was useful.

Then I pop the switch on the gurney which has a hydraulic type mechanism which allows it to rise on its own and I watch it slowly rise. The poor fucking gurney is so weighed down it takes a good five minutes to rise whereas with a normal sized personal it’s instantaneous.

Sweet, I am excited because now that he’s on the gurney I am almost done and once I am done I am going to strip the gown and gloves off and wash because I feel fucking disgusting and I am not suitable to be at the viewing I have to be at in the afternoon. Plus, air conditioning.

Once the gurney was up completely I locked it, tried to lock the body in (no seatbelt extender here!) and proceed to push the gurney up the ramp. The ramp is maybe 10 feet long and from there it is another 10 feet until you can turn into the double doors of the kitchen…So it’s not a huge distance at all.

Half way up the ramp, the gurney collapses under the weight. The body which was too big for the locking straps tumbles off next to the gurney.

I am about to lose my shit at this point.

Then the garage door opens and my coworkers are there with the new body. They look at me, look at the scene and start busting up laughing.

In hindsight it was funny, but at that moment I was furious so I removed my gloves and gown, took my shirt and jacket and went home to shower and try that day over again.
